column3: It directly exposes the worship of other-than God as lacking both warrant and knowledge, sharpening the focus's powerless object.
It gives the closest formulation: worshiping what cannot control either harm or benefit.
It repeats the harm-benefit challenge in Abraham's confrontation, adding a concrete prophetic dispute after the prior exact parallel.
It extends the incapacity of false objects from harm and benefit to provision and agency.
It situates the focus within the surah's account of a universal warning mission.
It treats calling a powerless other-than God as manifest, far-reaching error.
It adds the claimed intercessor rationale behind worshiping beings unable to harm or benefit.
It supplies a distinct local form of false worship: making one's own desire a deity.
Its brief utility test of idols is already substantially covered by the earlier harm-benefit parallels.
It contrasts false practice that harms without benefit, but does not address worship or misplaced support directly.
It turns the focus's diagnosis into a prohibition against calling on a powerless other-than God.
Exclusive worship and warning of punishment are relevant but add little specificity to the focus.
It expands the powerless-call theme by depicting it as a reversal away from divine guidance.
It continues the local statement of the messenger's role as bearer of warning and good news.
It depicts deniers recasting mutually supporting revelation as coordinated sorcery, a related misuse of support language.
The unbeliever's wish at judgment does not clarify false worship or support against the Lord.
It immediately shows the worshiped beings disowning the worshipers and tracing their ruin to forgetting remembrance.
It presents withdrawal from a community's false worship as the practical alternative to its dependence.
Concealed objectionable speech does not add a clear relation to the focus.
It locally directs people toward taking a way to their Lord, countering the focus's misplaced direction.
It vividly reverses the focus's support image: people make clan backing weightier than God and cast Him behind them.
It supplies an explicit refusal to become a supporter of wrongdoers, clarifying the moral direction of support.
Its repentance formula offers a broad remedy but does not develop the focus's worship or support claim.
It tests adopted gods against their inability to avert harm or rescue, complementing the focus's harm-benefit test.
It shows belief becoming useless at the sight of punishment, only indirectly related to the focus.
It gives the punishment of Satan's followers but does not clarify the false objects or support in the focus.
It sets exclusive worship of God as the alternative, even across a change of place.
It supplies a contrary use of mutual support: all beings cannot jointly produce the Quran's like.
It gives the immediate local response to the disbelievers: do not obey them and strive by the Quran.
Its statement that remembrance benefits believers only loosely contrasts with the focus's powerless objects.
Prayer, almsgiving, and divine approval do not clarify the focus.
Moses being given Aaron as a minister is a remote and different form of support.
Created livestock benefits invite gratitude, but this does not develop the false-worship claim.
Belief in revelation and its denial are relevant context but add little to the focus's precise language.
The opening question about what a people worship adds little after the more explicit earlier idol critiques.
Satanic private counsel causing limited harm is not a clear parallel to false worship.
It explicitly prohibits being a supporter of the disbelievers, directly countering the focus's final clause.
The divided seas and their barrier do not clarify false worship or support.
Beneficial remembrance is only a broad lexical contrast to the focus's benefit language.
It shows a person calling God in distress yet later setting up rivals, exposing unstable and misplaced dependence.
It is the local judgment scene that gathers worshipers with the beings worshiped besides God.
The limited harm of hostile opponents does not clarify the focus's worship relation.
Marital restrictions do not add a relation to the focus.
The people's admission that they worship idols is redundant with earlier, more explanatory cards.
Its joint mention of worshipers and worshiped beings offers only a partial parallel.
The delayed reckoning of human deeds does not clarify the focus.
The immediately preceding creation of human kinship heightens the contrast with turning from the Creator to powerless objects.
It states the single purpose of human and jinn creation as worship of God, supplying the governing alternative.
The marital provisions do not relate to the focus.
The dispersal of deeds gives judgment context but does not clarify false worship.
Its truth-and-falsehood parable uses benefit differently and only indirectly informs the focus.
Rules for debt documentation do not clarify the focus.
It adds the question whether idols can hear their worshipers' calls, testing responsive agency.
It culminates the harm-benefit denial in judgment, where no party controls either for another and the wrongdoers face the Fire.
Pharaoh's challenge to Moses to call his Lord does not clarify the focus's claim.
The withdrawal of the shadow does not add a relation to the focus.
Divine control of provision is a broad alternative to false dependence.
The historical punishment described does not clarify the focus's worship or support language.
The calf cannot answer, harm, or benefit, adding the failure of communicative as well as causal agency.
It depicts alleged objects of worship as unaware of the worshipers, denying any reciprocal religious relation.
It states in the same surah that adopted gods cannot create or control harm, benefit, death, life, or resurrection.
Repentance and transformed deeds provide only a general corrective context.
It distinguishes delivering guidance from possessing harm or right guidance, limiting even the messenger's authority.
It condemns calling another god without proof, directly pairing false invocation with failure.
The promise of Paradise does not clarify the focus.
The mention of mercy to Zachariah does not add a relation to the focus.
It shows prior false worship functioning as an obstacle that turns a person away from recognition.
Its rebuke of those and what they worship is largely redundant with the earlier Abrahamic exchange.
The believers' devotional identity does not clarify the focus's false worship claim.
Failure to humble oneself under punishment does not add a clear relation to the focus.
The believers' prayer to avert Hell does not clarify false worship or support.
Mutual support in sin and aggression is a different, only loosely related use of support.
Avoiding false powers and turning back to God supplies a direct alternative to the focus's worship.
The shadow's extension does not clarify the focus.
Abraham's call to worship God and be mindful of Him provides the central alternative to idol worship.
It joins false protectors with their inability to avail against Hell, extending the focus into judgment.
It distinguishes Satan's influence from authority over God's servants, refining the question of real backing and control.
The absence of intercession at judgment does not add enough beyond earlier powerlessness passages.
It explicitly denies alleged beings ownership, partnership, and any role as God's supporter, directly unpacking the focus's support language.
The disbelievers' arrogant demand to see angels or God gives nearby opposition context but no direct link.
It denies even the messenger independent possession of harm or benefit, strengthening the contrast with false deities.
Powerless intercessors repeat an explanation already supplied by earlier cards.
Questioning the promised time only remotely relates to the focus's issue of causal authority.
The general prophetic call to worship God is now largely covered by prior alternatives.
The statement that none but God can remove it lacks enough context to clarify the focus.
The receptive posture toward divine signs is a broad local contrast to disbelief.
Sharing punishment cannot benefit wrongdoers, but the connection is limited and late.
It rejects fabricated pagan regulations, offering only peripheral idolatry context.
The messenger's lack of independent harm-benefit control repeats the prior authority limitation.
Calling directly on God when harm strikes exposes the dependence that false worship obscures.
The direct address to disbelievers alone does not clarify the focus.
It says disbelievers cannot harm God, a partial reverse of the focus's claim that they back opposition to Him.
The revival sign does not clarify false worship or support.
The command to worship the shared Lord gives only a general alternative already represented.
The creation account does not add a direct relation to the focus.
It explicitly forbids worshiping those called besides God and commands submission to the Lord of all worlds.
The terse affirmation of humbled resurrection does not clarify the focus.
It reverses the supposed backing: the worshiped beings will reject their worship and become opponents.
The salutation upon messengers does not clarify the focus.
The command to worship the Lord of the city gives a general alternative but adds little after earlier monotheism cards.
It challenges whether beings that cannot create can be associated with the Creator, directly exposing false worship's reversal of agency.
It calls the alleged partners servants like their worshipers and tests whether they can answer an invocation.
It expressly states that those called besides God cannot help their worshipers or even help themselves.
It portrays the judgment-day separation of worshipers and their partners, who deny the worship relation.
It reserves removal of harm and bestowal of good to God, clarifying the authority falsely assigned to other beings.
It contrasts the true call answered by God with calls to others that receive no answer.
It describes beings invoked besides God as created rather than creators, directly undercutting their worship.
It shows the associators' alleged partners disowning them, developing the focus's failed backing into judgment.
It says those invoked besides God cannot remove or alter harm, an exact extension of the focus's powerless objects.
It shows that when harm strikes at sea all others invoked vanish from reliance, leaving God alone.
It commands the calling of alleged partners and shows that they neither answer nor provide rescue.
It identifies God alone as the deity whose knowledge encompasses all things, supplying the positive counterpart to powerless worship.
It argues that multiple gods would corrupt the ordered heavens and earth, extending the focus from incapacity to divine uniqueness.
It demonstrates the utter inability of all false gods together to create even a fly or recover what it takes.
It denies that idols control provision and redirects seekers of provision, worship, and gratitude to God.
It depicts the associators finding no intercessors among their alleged partners and repudiating those associations.
It asks whether any alleged partner creates, provides, causes death, or gives life, directly testing the authority worship attributes to them.
It presents the angels denying that people worshiped them, another judgment-day collapse of the claimed worship relation.
It states that those called besides God possess not even a date-stone membrane, cannot hear calls, and will deny association.
It notes that people take gods besides God in hope of help, then denies that those gods can help them.
It tests alleged partners against their inability to remove harm or withhold mercy when God wills either.
It rejects the command to worship another than God after the truth of exclusive worship has been made clear.
It limits intercession by those called besides God, preserving the distinction between alleged and warranted authority.
It challenges alleged partners to show what they created or share in within the heavens and earth.
It calls invocation of those who never answer and are unaware of their worship the furthest error, closely developing the focus.
It completes that scene by making the invoked beings enemies who reject their worshipers' worship.
It prohibits calling anyone alongside God in places devoted to worship, giving the direct normative alternative.
